TL;DR. This corrects only the two callbacks and their helper pins in the frozen row06/prep07 proposals. It grants no application, publication, or execution authority.

2026-10-28, Europe/Berlin. The full input specification remains at ../exception-diagnostics-proposal/SPEC-addendum.md except where this addendum narrows it. The review at ../exception-diagnostics-review/report.md is the correction basis. Exact read inputs and outputs are recorded in snapshot.json.

The diagnostic data shape remains the existing finite scalar record. Row probing is always null because the matched group_empty frame does not own that state. No owning-frame search is introduced. Every callback operation, including code matching, trace flag assignments, event filtering, and record construction, is inside its try boundary. A bound runner.Deadline or candidate.Deadline marks observer_failed and re-raises the same object with bare raise. An ordinary Exception marks observer_failed and returns None. Other BaseException control flow propagates. No new fields, caps, assertions, candidate behavior, or retained exception/frame objects are introduced. Existing teardown/output preservation remains byte exact.

Both operators change only the corrected helper byte count and SHA-256. Both workflows are byte exact copies. Selection, context, resources, fixed R fixture, two strict-JSON helper copies, source closure, storage envelope, and reserve remain exact. Consumed refs 04/05 remain untouched. Proposed 06/07 are not published by this correction.

synthetic_callback_regression.py defines six test methods. It parses the selected actual helper and compiles the actual nested observe FunctionDef plus the two actual scalar helpers inside a test-only closure. It never imports the supplied helper, runs a candidate, installs tracing, or launches external processes. Controlled fake frames exercise observable faults directly. Its Deadline double follows the bound runtimes' RuntimeError base class, so the ordering of the Deadline and Exception handlers matters.

Root must run the same script first with ../exception-diagnostics-proposal as its sole path argument and then with this directory. Both paths should be absolute. These are Synthetic callback checks only, with no Linux/native credit. Before/after results are not claimed here because root is the sole executor. Independent review remains required before any application or guarded diagnostic.

Confidence is High for the static byte comparisons recorded in snapshot.json and Medium for intended callback behavior pending root's checks. The claims assume the frozen proposal and bound runtimes are the sources later applied. Tracing can change timing, a captured event can be incidental, and observer failure can leave incomplete evidence. Keep final test outcomes beside observations and treat observer_failed, overflow, or missing evidence as inconclusive. This does not claim all asynchronous semantics are preserved or that timing perturbation is zero. Cost is one bounded helper correction and six cheap synthetic test methods. Before publication rollback discards this proposal; consumed attempts must remain preserved.

Next action belongs to root. Run the frozen before/after Synthetic checks and request fresh independent review. No runtime, worktree, Git, API, CI, ref, signing, or acceptance operation was performed here.
